headline: Q3 gross revenue surged 210% year-over-year, but footnote 4 reveals operating cash flow is negative $420M due to heavily uncollectible accounts receivable.
The board announced a record $2B share buyback program, entirely funded by issuing high-yield, variable-rate unsecured debt.
Earnings per share (EPS) beat estimates by $0.15, achieved exclusively by liquidating a core patent portfolio rather than operational sales.
The company declared a special dividend yield of 8%, while simultaneously reporting a payout ratio of 145% of free cash flow.
Top-line sales grew 40% in emerging markets, but days sales outstanding (DSO) increased from 45 days to 112 days, signaling channel stuffing.
Management boasts a 50% increase in EBITDA, completely omitting that capitalized software development costs were aggressively reclassified to hide R&D bloat.
Retail investors cheer a 5-for-1 stock split, ignoring the simultaneous 10-K filing showing a breach of standard debt covenants.
Customer acquisition doubled this quarter; however, customer acquisition cost (CAC) now exceeds the lifetime value (LTV) by a margin of 3 to 1.
The company announced a 'record profitable quarter,' but a deep dive into the cash flow statement shows they simply stopped paying tier-1 suppliers.
Gross margins expanded by 400 basis points, solely because the firm halted all routine maintenance on their primary manufacturing facilities.
Subscriptions grew by 1 million users, driven entirely by a 'first year free' promotion with zero recurring revenue guarantees.
The CEO announced year-over-year profit growth of 12%, though net debt ballooned by 400% to acquire a failing competitor.
Operating income reached an all-time high of $50M, while deferred revenue liabilities surged to $300M with no clear delivery timeline.
The company proudly reported hitting its EPS target, achieved by slashing the entire internal compliance and quality assurance budget.
A massive PR campaign highlights $1B in new contracted revenue, but the contracts allow clients to terminate at will with zero penalty.
Net income soared 50%, largely due to a one-time, non-recurring tax credit that will expire at the end of the current fiscal year.
The firm expanded its physical retail footprint by 30%, while same-store sales simultaneously contracted by 18%.
Management raised full-year guidance by 20% on the same day the CFO and Chief Accounting Officer abruptly resigned without explanation.
The company celebrated a 10% dividend hike, masking the fact they drew down their entire emergency revolving credit facility to pay it.
Record-breaking unit sales were reported this quarter, masking a 35% contraction in operating margins due to severe price-slashing.
The CEO's tweet about a 'revolutionary AI integration' gained 4 million likes, but independent engineering teardowns show the hardware overheats and fails 60% of the time.
Social media influencers are hyping a newly announced electric vehicle, though the company's primary lithium supplier just canceled their contract due to unpaid invoices.
A highly anticipated video game broke pre-order records, but internal leaks reveal severe execution friction and an unfinished core engine architecture.
The brand's new flagship smartphone is trending globally; meanwhile, manufacturing yield criteria at the primary foundry dropped to an abysmal 30%.
